analysis.title: Crossing the Duration Desert: Who will buy and who will supply the long end of the curve?
key_insights: Global gross duration supply peaked in 2021 at about USD6.5tn in 10-year equivalents. It is USD6.5tn in 2025 and USD5.6tn year-to-date, still elevated but slowing for all main issuers except China.
Net duration supply after buybacks and roll-down fell from USD3.3tn in 2021 to USD2.1tn in 2025. About USD1tn in 2026 would be the lowest since 2018.

The UK, Japan and the euro area add no new duration in 2026. The US and China each provide about half of net supply, and China's share is growing and should surpass the US. China's market is largely closed to global investors, so accessible duration is shrinking.

Sovereigns have shortened issuance duration by 1 to 3 years since the 2022 rate shock. Weighted issuance duration fell from 7 to 6 years in the US and from 11 to 8 years in the euro area, while China rose from 5 to 7 years.

Convenience yield has been under pressure since 2022 and is negative for the US, UK, France and Japan. Germany's remains positive. This favors more bills and fewer bonds, and the US 'Active Treasury Issuance' policy includes long-end buybacks of USD94bn in 2026.

Hedge funds are now dominant marginal buyers of duration, holding about USD6tn of sovereign exposure funded in repo. About 60% of the rise in US positions is linked to basis trades. Pensions and central banks are stepping back.

Hedge fund demand is leveraged, price sensitive and volatile. It adds a collateral and funding layer to monetary policy transmission, so central banks will favor reversible tools such as standing repo facilities. QE becomes a far out-of-the-money put.
QT is estimated to have raised 10y yields by 125bps in the euro area, 40bps in the US and 110bps in Japan. QT adds about 50bps more to long-end duration until 2033.

Corporate bonds are an imperfect substitute for sovereign duration. Hyperscaler IG issuance is about USD108bn in 2025, USD250bn expected in 2026 and close to USD400bn in 2027, roughly 10-20% of net Treasury supply. Meta's 30-year trades 75bps over Treasuries.
EU Bonds have preserved their convenience yield through recent turmoil and could position Europe as a high-quality long-duration supplier supporting the euro's international role.

The long end is cheap with an extra term premium of 50-100bps on a 30-year bond. Allianz expects a duration revival within 2-5 years from green, infrastructure, defense and ageing needs, which would erase the premium.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Still elevated but slowing for all main issuers except China.
Lowest since 2018, which supports a scarcity premium at the long end.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Compensation for crossing the duration desert, expected to vanish when scarcity hits.

macro_indicators.reading: USD94bn drag on net duration in 2026
macro_indicators.interpretation: USD75bn is in the 7 to 30 year segment, which reduces long-end supply.

trade_ideas.description: Buy long-dated (30-year) government bonds to capture 50-100bps extra term premium before duration scarcity returns
trade_ideas.rationale: A duration desert leaves the long end cheap, and a revival of demand within 2-5 years should erase the premium.
trade_ideas.risk: Hedge fund deleveraging and buyer-strike episodes could push yields higher, and further supply could follow stress episodes.

risk_factors: Abrupt hedge fund deleveraging and elevated repo specialness could erode the liquidity component of convenience yield.
Higher yields raise borrowing costs and could trigger more supply, reinforcing the stress.
Austerity-driven supply cuts could raise the specialness premium and destabilize money markets.
Traditional buyers such as pensions and central banks are retreating, and QE is now a tail tool.
Hyperscaler corporate issuance is concentrated at the very long end and could compete with sovereign supply.
charts_described: Figure 3 shows the 2y-10y term premium difference back to pre-QE levels at 50 to 100bps for the main issuers.
Figure 4 shows weighted issuance duration falling from 7 to 6 years in the US and from 11 to 8 years in the euro area, while China rose from 5 to 7 years.
Figure 9 shows repo-funded hedge fund exposure in US Treasuries rising sharply since 2022.
vol_and_positioning: Hedge funds hold about USD6tn of sovereign exposure financed in repo, concentrated in Treasury basis and swap spread trades, with a risk of rapid unwinds and deleveraging spirals.
56% of secondary-market euro government bond trading was hedge fund related in 2023, more than double 2018.
During QT 2022-2025 the share of Treasuries held by price-sensitive investors rose about 17pp while the 10-year term premium rose about 110bps.
Primary dealers are increasingly long government bond duration and charge a Basel III warehousing premium that penalizes long-dated issuance.
geopolitical: China's bond market is largely closed to global investors, so its growing share of net duration supply is not accessible to them.
The 2022 UK Gilt crisis and recent tension in European sovereign markets are cited as examples of leveraged positioning and buyer-strike risk.

tension_points.bull_case: The long end is cheap, offering 50-100bps extra term premium. Safe long-dated assets will be needed again for transition, defense and ageing within 2-5 years.
tension_points.bear_case: Demand is shifting to leveraged price-sensitive hedge funds, central banks retreat, and stress episodes can trigger buyer strikes and more supply.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A duration revival within 2-5 years removes the premium for those who wait, and a deleveraging spiral or buyer strike could widen yields first.

theme_stances.key_argument: Reduced net supply and weaker traditional demand leave the long end cheap, and scarcity will return within 2-5 years.
theme_stances.evidence: A duration desert is emerging from supply and demand side, leaving the long end cheap

theme_stances.key_argument: Leveraged relative-value demand is more volatile and fragile and complicates monetary policy transmission.
theme_stances.evidence: This makes the demand structure more volatile and more fragile.
